dedupe_keys.name: global flood depth damage functions jrc 2017 damage curves and maximum damage values by continent and country

description: A globally consistent database of flood depth-damage curves, published by the European Commission's Joint Research Centre in 2017 (JRC105688) and listed in the World Bank Data Catalog's Risk Data Library. It contains damage curves giving fractional damage as a function of water depth, with maximum damage values, for a range of assets and land-use classes. Normalised curves were developed for each continent from a broad literature survey, and country differences come from maximum damage values based on construction cost surveys by multinational construction companies, extended to all countries by regression on World Development Indicators. Coverage: all continents and countries, for a variety of assets and land-use classes. Access: the catalog entry offers the methodological report as a PDF and the curves as an xlsx workbook. Licence: Open Database License, per the World Bank catalog. Caveats: the curves are generic continental averages; the report itself gives guidance for adjusting them to local conditions such as urban or rural settings and building materials. Simulation uses: turning flood depth maps into direct building and content losses for supra-national or data-poor flood risk assessments. Related records: the USACE generic depth-damage functions and the FEMA NFIP claims data.
